additional_requirements: The binge eating occurs, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

S051.name: Rapid_Eating
S051.description: Eating much more rapidly than normal.
examples: Swallowing food without chewing it properly.
Eating continuously and rapidly to the point where it is difficult to breathe.
Eating so urgently that there is no time to taste the food.
Eating at a speed that surprises others.

S052.name: Eating_Until_Uncomfortably_Full
examples: Eating until the stomach feels distended to the point of bursting and pain.
Eating so much that it is difficult to even stand up or move.
Continuing to eat until feeling nauseous or like vomiting.
Unable to stop eating even though it is physically uncomfortable and painful.

S054.name: Eating_Alone_Due_to_Embarrassment
S054.description: Eating alone because of feeling embarrassed by how much one is eating.
examples: Eating only when alone because of fear that others will think strangely of the amount eaten.
Eating secretly after family members have gone to sleep.
Pretending to eat little in front of people, then binging when alone.
Locking the door or eating in a secret place like a car to avoid being seen eating.

S055.name: Negative_Affect_After_Binge
S055.description: Feeling disgusted with oneself, depressed, or very guilty afterward.
examples: Feeling unbearable disgust and self-loathing after binging.
Falling into extreme depression and self-criticism immediately after binging.
Feeling intense guilt and regret over the fact that I binged again.
Feeling shame that I am pathetic and have weak willpower after binging.

info.persona: Roy Trim fuses a disciplined engineering mindset with hands‑on craftsmanship, turning precision at the CNC machine into meticulous garden tending, woodworking, and habit‑driven community service—though they can’t resist an extra slice of peach cobbler on Sunday evenings.
info.professional_persona: Roy Trim, a veteran manufacturing specialist with three decades of high‑speed assembly line and CNC expertise, leverages his methodical lean‑manufacturing mindset and passion for mentoring apprentices to pursue a shift‑supervisor role, where their practical problem‑solving and safety‑first ethos drive continuous improvement initiatives.
info.cultural_background: Roy was raised in the vibrant African‑American community of Newark before his family settled in Belleville, New Jersey. His upbringing was steeped in the traditions of family gatherings, Sunday church services, and the soulful sounds of gospel music that accompanied many of his formative years. The values of perseverance, respect for elders, and the importance of community service—hallmarks of his cultural heritage—have shaped his identity. Though he did not complete a college degree, his parents emphasized the importance of education and hard work, instilling in him a practical, resourceful mindset. Roy’s cultural background also includes a strong connection to the civil‑rights legacy of the region, which informs his commitment to fairness and mentorship in the workplace.
info.hobbies_and_interests: During his free time, Roy enjoys activities that blend structure with creativity. He tends his modest backyard garden, growing tomatoes, peppers, and herbs, and finds the routine of planting and pruning grounding. Woodworking projects—building furniture and small wooden toys—allow him to apply his mechanical skills in a leisurely way. He is an avid fan of NFL and NBA games, especially following the New York Giants and Brooklyn Nets, and often watches games with family and friends. Cooking Southern comfort food, especially dishes passed down from his grandparents, is a weekend ritual that brings the family together. Roy is active in his local Baptist church, participating in the choir and volunteering for community outreach programs. He also enjoys occasional fishing trips with his wife and reading historical biographies, which satisfy his curiosity about past events while offering a structured, disciplined reading habit.
info.sports_persona: Roy Trim is a devoted fan of the New York Giants and Brooklyn Nets, never missing a weekend game on the big screen with family, participates in a local amateur softball league, and supports seasonal fishing trips with their spouse along the Atlantic coast as a complement to their sports enthusiasm.
info.arts_persona: Roy Trim expresses artistic side through singing in the Baptist church choir, woodworking handcrafted toys inspired by folk art traditions, listening to the soulful gospel harmonies of Mahalia Jackson and the storytelling country ballads of Johnny Cash, and occasionally attending a regional theater production of "The Glass Menagerie" when time allows.
info.travel_persona: Roy Trim prefers road‑trip itineraries that blend fishing expeditions with family history, having already explored the Florida Keys for tarpon fishing, taken a nostalgic weekend drive to Savannah’s historic district, and now dreaming of a guided fly‑fishing adventure on Montana’s Madison River, all while balancing a modest travel budget.
info.culinary_persona: Roy Trim’s culinary repertoire centers on Southern comfort dishes like crispy fried chicken, buttery cornbread, and simmered collard greens seasoned with fresh basil and thyme from their backyard garden, and while they pride themselves on following grandma's gumbo recipe, they sometimes over‑salt the stew in their enthusiasm to perfect the flavor.

info.persona: Belinda Naab blends a competitive edge with pragmatic curiosity, nurturing a garden, budgeting a PTA, and quilting in equal measure, yet sometimes lets a penchant for perfectionism lead to late‑night spreadsheet marathons and a refusal to try untested health fads, and they occasionally forget to water indoor plants during bridge tournaments.
info.professional_persona: Belinda Naab, a community‑centered organizer and hands‑on problem‑solver, blends pragmatic curiosity with competitive precision to manage the PTA’s treasury, spearhead the neighborhood pollinator garden, and dispense DIY home‑repair advice at the senior center, all while they keep a meticulous ledger of community projects.
info.cultural_background: Belinda grew up in a traditional white Southern family in coastal Alabama, surrounded by the rhythms of Gulf life and a close‑knit church community. Her upbringing emphasized hospitality, self‑reliance, and respect for nature, especially the ocean and wetlands. Family gatherings centered around home‑cooked meals, gospel music, and storytelling, instilling a strong sense of community and pride in regional traditions. She has been shaped by the cultural heritage of the Deep South, including a love for Southern cuisine, a reverence for church as a social hub, and participation in local festivals such as the Baldwin County Fair. While she embraces new ideas, she remains rooted in the values of modesty, hard work, and neighborly support that characterize her cultural background.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Belinda enjoys a mix of solitary and social activities that reflect her balanced personality. She spends mornings tending to her garden, experimenting with seasonal vegetables and native flowers. Reading historical fiction and biographies satisfies her curiosity about the past while offering an escape. She frequently bakes and cooks Southern comfort foods, often incorporating healthier ingredients. Quilting and sewing provide a creative outlet, and she occasionally participates in local craft fairs. Birdwatching along the nearby wetlands, walking on the Gulf beaches, and attending church socials keep her connected to nature and community. Belinda also enjoys playing bridge at the senior center, where her competitive streak shines, and she volunteers as a treasurer for the local PTA, using her organizational skills.
info.sports_persona: Belinda Naab, a devoted fan of the New Orleans Saints and Atlanta Braves, stays active by joining the local senior walking club on beach mornings, playing bridge competitively at the community center, and birdwatching during early‑season migrations, and they often celebrate a Saints victory with a potluck for friends, balancing low‑impact exercise with a love for team spirit.
info.arts_persona: Belinda Naab, an avid quilter and reader of Margaret Mitchell and Hilary Mantel, cultivates creative expression through intricate patchwork inspired by Southern folk motifs, attends church gospel concerts featuring the Atlanta Symphony Chorus, and enjoys the timeless songwriting of Dolly Parton and the classic brushwork of Winslow Homer, and they often incorporate botanical prints from their garden into quilt designs.
info.travel_persona: Belinda Naab, who prefers leisurely planning over spontaneous bursts, dreams of a short Gulf‑Coast cruise visiting historic ports like Mobile and New Orleans, while also yearning to explore the culinary markets of Barcelona, and they budget travel costs within their modest retirement fund to ensure each trip remains affordable.
info.culinary_persona: Belinda Naab, a master of Southern comfort cuisine with a health‑conscious twist, delights in preparing shrimp and grits with smoked paprika, collard greens seasoned with kale and apple cider vinegar, and low‑sugar pecan pie, while they often experiment with heirloom tomatoes and fresh herbs from their garden, adding a personal touch to each dish.

info.persona: Dennis Courville, a 19‑year‑old aspiring project manager, merges competitive team sports, meticulous planning, and a love for guitar and gaming into a driven yet occasionally skeptical mindset that thrives on group challenges and practical ambition, and they constantly seek new ways to apply their organized instincts.
info.professional_persona: Dennis Courville, an aspiring junior project manager, blends their Business Administration studies and Mechanical Engineering minor with hands‑on robotics club leadership, using Excel pivot tables, Python scripts, and CAD basics to orchestrate student engineering projects through detailed Gantt charts, while their competitive edge pushes them to meet every deadline with precision.
info.cultural_background: Born and raised in Latrobe, Pennsylvania, Dennis grew up in a middle‑class, White family with French‑Canadian ancestry evident in the Courville surname. The town’s strong working‑class roots, love of high‑school football, and community pride have shaped his values of hard work, reliability, and teamwork. He regularly attends Steelers games and local fairs, and his family traditions include gathering for Sunday dinner and participating in the Westmoreland County Fair. The region’s blend of industrial history and Appalachian culture has fostered his practical outlook, competitive edge, and appreciation for community cohesion.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Outdoors and group activities energize Dennis. He regularly plays intramural basketball and ultimate frisbee, enjoying the competitive spirit of team sports. He loves hiking the Allegheny foothills and occasional camping trips with friends. Music is a personal outlet; he teaches himself guitar and occasionally jams at local open‑mic nights. He is an avid participant in tabletop board‑gaming sessions and video‑gaming evenings, where his strategic thinking shines. He also volunteers at the Latrobe Food Bank and helps organize community events, reflecting his sociable nature and desire to stay connected with his hometown.
info.sports_persona: Dennis Courville dominates intramural basketball and thrives in ultimate frisbee matches with the Southwest PA Ultimate Frisbee Club, roots for the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sundays, and they use weekend hikes in the Allegheny foothills as cardio cross‑training, balancing competitive play with outdoor endurance.
info.arts_persona: Dennis Courville strums acoustic renditions of "John Mayer" at The Black Cat's open‑mic nights, dives into strategic board‑gaming marathons while quoting Wes Anderson's "The Grand Budapest Hotel", and powers up with Foo Fighters tracks before heading to the basketball court, merging musical, cinematic, and gaming passions into their creative outlet, and they often invite friends over for impromptu jam sessions.
info.travel_persona: Dennis Courville crafts meticulous Google Docs itineraries for weekend trips to Ohiopyle State Park, saves diligently for a spring road trip to New York City's museum corridor, and they dream of a future backpacking adventure through Japan's tech hubs, balancing a love for exploration with the constraints of a student budget.
info.culinary_persona: Dennis Courville enjoys a quick pepperoni pizza slice after late‑night study sessions, but also cooks a hearty spaghetti carbonara with pancetta and Parmesan, and they prepare homemade trail mix of almonds, dried cranberries, and chocolate chips for hikes in the Alleghenies, showcasing a mix of convenience and culinary skill.
